subject.title: Browser tool needs a CDP/IME text insertion action for contenteditable editors like X composer

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser act kind for native/CDP text insertion, and what driver, focus, and unsupported-behavior contract should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a model-facing browser action is public API and the existing Playwright and Chrome MCP paths need a maintainer-owned contract before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Define a focused native text action
options.body: Add one explicit act kind for native text insertion, implement CDP support where available, document unsupported drivers, and require live IME proof before closing.

options.title: Defer for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers or the reporter provide a real X/contenteditable IME reproduction that fixes the final action contract.

options.title: Handle only adjacent noVNC input
options.body: Leave browser act unchanged and treat non-Latin input through the separate noVNC clipboard issue, accepting that rich-editor automation remains unsolved.

recommendation.title: Define a focused native text action
recommendation.body: Add one explicit act kind for native text insertion, implement CDP support where available, document unsupported drivers, and require live IME proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current contract history is the browser /act route unification that this new action would extend.
